text:
frank: Opened a docs PR to reconcile the response id shown in examples vs the header we actually emit. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1433

leah: What's the mismatch?

frank: Examples show a top-level `id` in the JSON response, but our servers also return `X-Request-Id` (dash-case) as a response header. Some SDK snippets read resp.id while others check resp.headers['x-request-id']. That confused adopters about which is canonical.

omar: Oof. We should pick a canonical surface for the docs and show how SDKs map the header/body consistently.

frank: Proposed in PR: document `X-Request-Id` in OpenAPI under components/headers with a description and add `x-sdk-field: id` so codegen can expose it as resp.id in generated clients. Keep the JSON body `id` (unchanged) but add a deprecation note on body-only consumers that rely on id being present in body for proxies that may strip headers.

leah: I like documenting the header explicitly. Can we also add a short snippet showing how to read from headers in each SDK for people who want low-level access?

frank: Done. PR adds minimal examples for curl (showing the header in response), Python (resp.id and resp.headers access), and JS. Also added a migration blurb: "Prefer resp.id (SDK-mapped) or X-Request-Id header for tracing; if you depended on only header presence keep using headers but SDKs will expose id for convenience."

docs-bot: Deploy preview: https://deploy-preview.docs.redwood.ai/1433  header and SDK snippets updated.

omar: Small nit: canonical header casing in docs should be `X-Request-Id` (capital R and I). Backend treats headers case-insensitive but examples should be consistent.

frank: Using `X-Request-Id` in examples and OpenAPI header name. Also added `deprecated` flags to any example that relied on header-only mapping without showing body id.

leah: Tests: I'll update our integration tests that assert `id` presence to also assert `X-Request-Id` header is set. For SDK tests, I'll verify resp.id is populated.

omar: For streaming SSE, do we need to include an `event-id` field? There's a streaming client that relied on `id` in each event.

frank: Good catch. PR updates SSE docs: each SSE final `done` event includes `event_id` and the final JSON body includes `id`. Added migration guidance for streaming clients: use the event `id` field or header when available.

leah: LGTM. Reviewer checklist in PR description: [ ] add OpenAPI components/headers (done) [ ] add x-sdk-field for codegen (done) [ ] update curl/python/js snippets (done) [ ] update SSE docs (done) [ ] update tests (in flight)

frank: Merging once CI is green. Thanks for the quick reviews. :rocket:

---

Example snippets from PR:

Curl request/response:
``
$ curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"summarize this"}'

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Request-Id: req_01F...
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":"gen_01F...","output":"..."}
``

Python SDK snippet:
``
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1", input="x")
print(resp.id)  # SDK maps X-Request-Id/header -> resp.id when available
print(resp.headers.get('x-request-id'))  # low-level header access
``

Migration note (short):
- The platform emits both a response header `X-Request-Id` and a JSON body `id` for traceability. Docs now document the header in OpenAPI and SDKs map the header to resp.id for convenience. If you rely on proxies that strip headers, continue to read the JSON `id`. Streaming events include an `event_id` for per-chunk correlation
__notes: Slack thread: concise coordination for docs PR standardizing response id header vs body id and SDK mapping
